title: eBay.com Customer Support: Day in the Life in Salt Lake City 2014
description: This video shows the culture and work environment of eBay.com's customer support teams in Salt Lake City, Utah. This is a good representation of eBay's culture overall in their call centers.

asr.full_text: music eBay is a people company. It's a very exciting company. Do you have an item number for me? We'll setup a compatibility bill. eBay is a place where constant change happens. We are at the forefront of eCommerce so if we're not changing then it means we're staying stagnant. If you're uncomfortable, being able to be flexible, then this might not be the environment for you. The perfect eBay employee is someone very upbeat. And you really want to be passionate and excited. You can organize them on the same level. A people person. I mean, they're inquisitive, that they're self-motivated. I definitely want to make sure we get you taken care of, so I want to get over PayPal. I knew day one. I told my wife I found the job I'm going to retire from. You are the face of eBay here. You are the front line when you are talking to the customer. Our tone, how we respond to their needs, indicates what we are representing as far as the company and our culture. You have to be willing to research trying to understand what could be the underlying problem or whatever frustration the customer has. You know, it's Never taken it personally. and just, once that calls over and you just pretty much shake it off and start fresh. To give the best service... You can't be a robot, you can't read a script, you have to react to the other person on the end of the line. We talked to over 10 million people in North America a year so, we have 10 million opportunities to make a difference to those folks. I first got connected with eBay selling baseball cards. Now I'm selling shoes. We've sold hundreds of thousands of shoes on eBay. I feel like they know who I am and they understand our business's needs and wants. So I see this relationship lasting hopefully for a very long time. This is a beautiful area of the country. The weather here is wonderful. We just moved into this fabulous new LEED-certified building. It's 221, twenty one thousand square feet Oh this inside is so pretty I love it, love it, love it There's solar energy there's recycling I ride my bike to work pretty much every day During the winter, I have my own garage for my bike So it's nice, it holds about a hundred and eighty bikes We are located next to Mass Transit. eBay reimburses you for the public transportation every month. My favorite amenity is the restaurant. The food is amazing. It's very good and healthy, and you have so many choices. One of the biggest things is the fitness center. The fact that I get a free membership, just by being an employee as the fitness center, the fact that I get a free membership just by being an employee. The game room is awesome. We try to make it as fun as possible. eBay takes very good care of their new hires. They make sure their thoroughly trained, adequate and able to take any customer calls that should come in. TAMARA EBAERMANN, EBAERMANN, TROYAL TEAM, POMPATRON, SCOTTSDALE, And it arrived completely broken, and it looked like it had been glued back together. ELLEN DURRINGTON, ELKESTER STORE, To be a coach for eBay is a relatively new role, but a very critical and dynamic role within the company. DAVID VEINFELD, DEV VENDOR, CO-HOUSING CONSUMER I DEFINITELY want to help you out with this and since you're not wanting to pay the return. DANNA CHAMBER, STORE SHIP TEAM, T wanting to pay the return- To have that mentor really has helped the teammates to really drive their success. I don't think it was your normal confident tone. I think that she was definitely in the driver's seat wouldn't you agree. I think recognition is always important because it is validating. And we have recognition programs that are just a simple card that you can send to a teammate all the way up to the Global Best of the Best. If you do the work and put your time in, you'll excel. If you want to go somewhere, you have the opportunity to do so. We are a global company but we feel like a Mom-and-Pop shop. There are no doors so management is right there on the floor with us and so the culture here is really more like a community. At the end of the day, if I can have a customer who might come in frustrated but leave the call happy and satisfied with Revolution, I feel like I've done a good job. This work is very hard and it's very demanding, but it's worth it because of those connections. We're all in this together. We are all Igbe. We create experiences our customers love. Come to join us!
